data.subtitle: Honourable Chief Judge, Gombe State
data.bio: Honourable Justice Halima S. Mohammed, born on May 3, 1963, in Gombe State, Nigeria, is the Chief Judge of Gombe State. She is a distinguished legal professional with a Bachelor of Law from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, an LL.M from the University of Jos, and over 37 years of experience in the legal field. She began her legal career in 1987 as State Counsel II, and later appointed as Magistrate. She was Deputy Chief Registrar Gombe State High Court before her appointment as a High Court Judge in 2001. She was appointed Acting Chief Judge of Gombe State in October 2022. Her exemplary performance led to her confirmation as the Substantive Chief Judge on 16th February, 2023, where she has implemented legal reforms, improved court efficiency, and demonstrated a commitment to justice and fairness. Justice Halima S. Mohammed has attended various conferences and workshops nationally and internationally. She is known for her integrity, dedication, and contributions to legal scholarship and community engagement, making her a beacon of justice in Gombe State. She is widowed and has children and grandchildren.

data.tagline: The Head of Administration and Custodian of Judicial Records
data.overview:
General Administrative Function

The Office of the Chief Registrar (CR) serves as the administrative head of the Gombe State Judiciary. The Chief Registrar, supported by Deputy Chief Registrars, oversees the implementation of judicial policies and the day-to-day coordination of all departments and directorates.

This office ensures that the vision of the Honorable Chief Judge is translated into efficient administrative action, maintaining the highest standards of discipline and productivity across the entire workforce.
data.headQuote: Our office is dedicated to providing the administrative excellence required to support the delivery of swift and impartial justice.

The Directorate of Admin & Finance is the central administrative and financial hub of the Gombe State Judiciary. It is responsible for the strategic management of the court's budget, expenditure, and overall administrative logistics.

Our primary mandate is to ensure that the Judiciary operates with financial transparency and that all departments have the necessary resources to perform their judicial functions effectively. We handle everything from budget preparation to payroll management and auditing.
data.headQuote: Transparency and accountability are the watchwords of our fiscal administration, ensuring the Judiciary's independence through sound management.

data.summary: Facilitating peaceful and timely conflict resolution through mediation, conciliation, and arbitration outside traditional litigation.
data.heading: Alternative Dispute Resolution
data.tagline: Promoting Harmonious Settlements through Mediation and Conciliation
data.overview:
The Directorate of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) provides an innovative approach to justice by offering parties a platform to resolve their disputes amicably without the rigors and adversarial nature of traditional litigation.

By utilizing Mediation, Conciliation, and Arbitration, the ADR center helps to reduce the caseload of the courts while preserving relationships between parties. It is a faster, more cost-effective, and confidential way to achieve a "win-win" outcome for all involved.
data.headQuote: Justice is not only found in a judgment, but also in the peace that comes from a mutual agreement.

data.summary: Legal research resources, law reports, and archival services.
data.heading: Directorate of Library
data.tagline: The Custodian of Legal Knowledge and Judicial Research
data.overview:
The Directorate of Library serves as the intellectual hub of the Gombe State Judiciary. It is dedicated to providing comprehensive legal resources, law reports, and research materials to support the Honorable Judges, legal practitioners, and judicial staff in the efficient delivery of justice.

Our collection spans across traditional law volumes and modern digital legal databases, ensuring that the court remains abreast of the latest judicial precedents and legislative changes both locally and internationally.

Core Services

  • Provision of Law Reports (NWLR, SC, etc.)
  • Access to E-Library and Online Legal Databases
  • Archiving of Gombe State Edicts and Laws
  • Legal Research Support for Judicial Officers
data.headQuote: Our mission is to empower the bench and bar with accurate legal information through a well-curated collection of global and local legal resources.

data.summary: Processing of case files, court registries, and dispute documentation.
data.heading: Directorate of Litigation
data.tagline: Managing Case Life-Cycles and the Enforcement of Justice
data.overview:
The Directorate of Litigation is the heartbeat of the court's daily operations. It handles the filing, processing, and management of all civil and criminal cases brought before the High Court. From the moment a case is filed to its final resolution, this directorate ensures the record is handled with the utmost integrity.

It acts as the primary interface between the legal practitioners and the judiciary, ensuring that all processes filed comply with the High Court Rules.
data.headQuote: Our commitment is to ensure that every case is processed with speed and every judgment is given the pathway to enforcement.

data.more:
The Execution Unit

The Execution Unit is the enforcement arm of the Directorate of Litigation. Its primary mandate is to ensure that the orders and judgments delivered by the Court are carried out to the letter.

  • Attachment and Sale of Property
  • Execution of Possession Orders
  • Service of Garnishee Orders

data.tagline: Supervising the Engine Room of Summary Jurisdiction
data.overview:
The Directorate of Magistracy is responsible for the overall administrative coordination of all Magistrate Courts in Gombe State. Magistrate Courts handle a significant volume of both criminal and civil cases, serving as a primary pillar of justice in our urban and rural communities.

This directorate ensures that Magistrate Courts are adequately staffed, resourced, and functioning in accordance with the Magistrate Court Laws and Rules, providing oversight for the efficient disposal of cases.
data.headQuote: Our mission is to ensure that the Magistrate Courts remain efficient, accessible, and firm in the administration of summary justice.

The Directorate of Personnel is responsible for the recruitment, development, and welfare of the entire workforce of the Gombe State Judiciary. We ensure that the court is staffed by competent, disciplined, and motivated individuals dedicated to the service of justice.

Beyond administrative duties, the directorate manages career progression, retirement benefits, and personnel records to maintain a high standard of professional ethics within the organization.
data.headQuote: Our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to fostering a professional environment where merit and integrity thrive.

data.summary: Service of court processes, summons, and official notices.
data.heading: Directorate of Process
data.tagline: Facilitating Legal Notice and Judicial Enforcement
data.overview:
The Directorate of Process (Sheriff's Department) is responsible for the formal service of all court processes, including summons, writs, and notices. It ensures that all parties in a legal matter are properly notified in accordance with the law, which is a fundamental requirement for a fair hearing.

The directorate operates through a network of Bailiffs and Process Servers who carry out the physical delivery of documents and the enforcement of court orders across the state.
data.headQuote: Service of process is the foundation of jurisdiction. We ensure that justice starts with a proper and lawful notice.

data.tagline: Driving Judicial Reform through Data and Strategic Insight
data.overview:
The Directorate of Research, Planning, and Statistics (RP&S) is vital for the evidence-based management of the Gombe State Judiciary. We specialize in the collection and analysis of judicial data to monitor case flow, judge performance, and court congestion.

Our department is responsible for producing the Annual Judicial Report, developing long-term strategic plans, and conducting legal research that aids the administration of justice and policy formulation.

data.subtitle: Gombe State High Court of Justice
data.body:
Established

Established as a Superior Court of Record following the creation of Gombe State in 1996, under Section 270 of the 1999 Constitution.

Our Mission

To ensure an efficient and transparent administration of justice through the rule of law and judicial independence.

Constitutional Mandate

The High Court of Justice is a key component of the Gombe State Judiciary. While the Judiciary encompasses all courts in the state, the High Court exercises original and appellate jurisdiction as defined by law.

Original Jurisdiction

The Court has the power to hear and determine any civil proceedings in which the existence or extent of a legal right, power, duty, liability, privilege, interest, obligation or claim is in issue. It also handles serious criminal matters.

Appellate Jurisdiction

We serve as a vital link in the justice chain by hearing appeals from the Magistrates’ Courts. This ensures that every citizen has the right to a fair review of lower court decisions.

Administrative Leadership

Beyond the bench, the High Court is supported by a robust administrative framework led by the Chief Registrar.

  • The Chief Registrar:

    The Chief Accounting Officer and head of administration for the High Court.

  • The Probate Registry:

    Responsible for the administration of estates, wills, and letters of administration.

  • The Litigation Department:

    Manages the filing, processing, and archiving of all court processes.

Institutional Hierarchy

The Gombe State High Court operates under a structured hierarchy ensuring accountability at every level of the registry and judicial staff.

Our History & Evolution

A legacy of justice since the creation of Gombe State.

1996
Establishment

Following the creation of Gombe State by the then Federal Military Government, the High Court of Justice was established to provide a superior court of record for the new state.

1999
Constitutional Transition

The court transitioned under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, solidifying its status under Section 270 as a pillar of the state's democracy.

Present
Digital Transformation

Today, the High Court continues to expand with multiple judicial divisions across the state, integrating technology to enhance the speed of justice delivery.

data.subtitle: Fast, Informal, and Inexpensive Access to Justice
data.body:
• Eligibility
  • The Process
  • Forms & Reports
  • Designated Courts

What is the Small Claims Court?

The Small Claims Court is a specialized magisterial court designed to provide a fast, informal, and inexpensive way to resolve liquidated money disputes (debts) not exceeding ₦3,000,000. The entire process is strictly time-bound to ensure judgment is delivered within 60 days.

How to File a Case:
  1. Issue Demand: Serve the debtor with Form SCA 1 and wait 7 days.
  2. File Complaint: If unpaid, visit the Registry with Form SCA 2 and your evidence.
  3. Pay Fees: Pay the prescribed filing fees at the designated bank or point.
  4. Await Service: The Court Sheriff will serve the Summons on the defendant.
Key Requirements
  • Maximum Claim: ₦3,000,000
  • Claim Type: Liquidated Money (Debts/Damages)
  • Parties: Must live or do business in Gombe State
  • Timeline: 60-Day Fast-Track

Are you eligible?

This court handles simple debt recovery and liquidated damages cases.

Is your claim for money only, and is it ₦3,000,000 or less?

Know Your Fees

The Gombe State Small Claims Court is designed to be affordable. Below is a summary of the standardized filing costs in accordance with the current Practice Direction.

Note: All payments must be made at the designated bank gallery within the Court Complex or via the official E-Payment portal.
Service Item Fee (₦)
Filing Fee (Claims up to ₦1,000,000) 1,000.00
Filing Fee (Claims ₦1,000,001 - ₦5,000,000) 2,500.00
Service of Process (Per Party within jurisdiction) 500.00
Certificate of Judgment / Order 500.00
Administrative/Hearing Fee Free
* Fees are subject to periodic review by the Honorable Chief Judge.

From Demand to Judgment

The Small Claims process is designed to be completed within 60 days.

1
Letter of Demand

Claimant serves a formal demand (Form SCA 1) on the Defendant.

2
Filing Claim

If no payment in 7 days, file Form SCA 2 at the Registry.

3
Service

Sheriff serves the summons on the Defendant within 7 days.

4
Trial/Hearing

Trial is conducted daily or weekly with minimal adjournments.

5
Judgment

Delivered within 14 days of the conclusion of the hearing.

Served with a Summons?

If you have been served with a Small Claims Summons, you are the Defendant. You must act quickly—usually within 7 days—to prevent a judgment being entered against you in your absence.

Admission

If you owe the money, you can admit the claim and suggest a payment plan using Form SCA 5.

Defense

If you dispute the claim, file a Points of Defense explaining why you do not owe the money.

Common Legal Defenses
  • Debt Already Paid: You have proof of payment (receipts/transfers).
  • Statute of Barred: The debt is too old to be legally enforced.
  • Goods/Services Not Delivered: The contract was never fulfilled by the claimant.
  • Wrong Defendant: You are not the person who entered the agreement.
  • Counter-Claim: The claimant actually owes *you* money.
